diagnosis.root_cause: orders_pk_index[ok] (240MB, random access) looked up independently in 8 branches (Q3,Q5,Q7,Q8,Q9,Q10,Q12,Q21) per row. Since Q5 has no pre-filter, this means 8 redundant random accesses into a cache-exceeding array per row x 60M rows. Similarly o_orderdate[orow], o_custkey[orow], and s_nationkey[sk-1] are redundantly loaded across 5-6 branches each. Compiler cannot CSE these due to intervening unordered_map writes that may alias.
diagnosis.memory_footprint: orders_pk_index: 60M x 4B = 240MB (6x L3). o_orderdate: 60MB. o_custkey: 60MB. All random access per row.

edit_summary: Hoisted orders_pk_index[ok], o_orderdate[orow], o_custkey[orow], and s_nationkey[sk-1] lookups to compute once per row and reuse across all 8 branches. Added __restrict__ qualifiers on all column pointers to enable compiler CSE/vectorization. Deferred loading of rarely-needed columns (tax, returnflag, linestatus, quantity) to inside their specific branches.
expected_improvement: ~15-25% scan latency reduction from eliminating 7 redundant random accesses per row into a 240MB array exceeding L3 cache
